clue.text: Very long online movie?

parts.note: E- is the prefix for electronic or online, as in email
a pic is an informal word for a film or movie

explanation.surface: A question about an endless film streamed on the internet.
explanation.definitionFit: An epic is a lengthy work, so as an adjective it describes something on a grand, drawn-out scale.

clue.text: A force within the TA on my year off

indicators.note: off here means gone wrong or out of order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A soldier in the Territorial Army mentions a year away from service.
explanation.walkthrough: The TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve; its mounted regiments were historically called the yeomanry.
explanation.definitionFit: The yeomanry was a volunteer cavalry force, later absorbed into the Territorial Army as reserve units.

clue.text: Crazy fast driver starts to joyride, eventually hospitalising us

indicators.note: starts to means only the opening letter of each following word is used

explanation.surface: A reckless joyrider whose wild driving ends up putting the speaker in hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Bible, Jehu 'driveth furiously' (2 Kings 9:20), so his name became a jocular term for a reckless driver.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical king famed for furious chariot driving gives his name to any wild, speeding motorist.

clue.text: Cultural artefacts from travelling fair somewhere in Galilee

indicators.note: travelling means the letters move about into a new order

parts.note: Cana is the village in Galilee where Jesus turned water into wine

explanation.surface: A souvenir stall at a touring fair offering items from the Holy Land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'travelling fair' reads as a funfair on tour, but 'travelling' scrambles FAIR into AFRI.
explanation.definitionFit: Africana are objects, books and art relating to Africa, collected as a cultural category.

clue.text: Fellow runs with topless servant girl in cross-channel race

parts.note: R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs

indicators.note: topless means the word loses its top, i.e. its first letter

parts.note: a wench is an old word for a serving girl or maid

explanation.surface: A man running with a scantily clad maid in some cross-channel contest.
explanation.definitionFit: The people of France are a race, in the old sense of a nation, just across the English Channel.

clue.text: Ornament for displaying flowers, Jan 31? That is organised

indicators.note: organised means the gathered letters are put into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written, the short form of January
the number points to the answer of clue 31 across, used here as letters
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: Someone planning a floral ornament for the last day of January.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jan 31' looks like a date, but 31 is a cross-reference to the answer at 31 across, whose letters join JAN and IE in the anagram signalled by 'organised'.
explanation.definitionFit: A jardiniere is a decorative pot or stand for holding plants and flowers.

clue.text: As Iceland released worsening ash, you'd each head for the Channel

indicators.note: each head means the first letter of every one of the preceding words is taken

explanation.surface: Pilots heading for the English Channel as Iceland's volcano poured out ash.
explanation.walkthrough: This recalls the 2010 Eyjafjallajökull eruption, whose ash cloud closed European airspace; 'the Channel' looks like the sea but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An airway is a passage for air, such as the windpipe, so it is a channel in that sense.

clue.text: Component of early reed instrument

indicators.note: Component of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Something that formed part of a primitive reed instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A lyre is a stringed instrument of ancient Greece, a small harp.

clue.text: Grievance leads to volcanic eruption by Jimmy

parts.note: Jimmy Riddle is rhyming slang for piddle, so a jimmy is a wee

indicators.note: leads to means the opening letters of the following words are taken

explanation.surface: A complaint that some volcanic eruption is caused by a man called Jimmy.
explanation.walkthrough: Jimmy Riddle is British rhyming slang for piddle, hence a wee; 'by' here just means next to.
explanation.definitionFit: A peeve is a pet grievance or annoyance, something that irritates.

clue.text: Touring African country, score twice for punctiliousness

indicators.note: touring means going around, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: a score is twenty, so twice that is forty
Mali is a country in West Africa

explanation.surface: A sports team touring an African nation, scoring twice, praised for being punctilious.
explanation.definitionFit: Formality is strict observance of rules and etiquette, close in sense to punctiliousness.

clue.text: Part of service university held in public

indicators.note: held in means one piece is enclosed by the other

parts.note: common land is public, shared by all
uni is the informal short form of university

explanation.surface: Part of a university ceremony that takes place in public.
explanation.definitionFit: Holy Communion is the Eucharist, a central part of a Christian church service.

clue.text: Choice of window seats? Divine!

indicators.note: Choice of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An exclamation of delight at being offered the window seats on a plane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Divine!' reads as praise but is a verb: to find water by divining.
explanation.definitionFit: To dowse is to search for underground water or minerals with a rod, which is to divine.

clue.text: Criticise expert primarily advocating non-specific cure

parts.note: to pan is to criticise harshly
an ace is an expert

indicators.note: primarily means the first letter only is used

explanation.surface: A critic attacks an expert who recommends a vague, all-purpose remedy.
explanation.definitionFit: A panacea is a supposed remedy for all ills, so it treats nothing in particular.

clue.text: It could be a sea anemone, parrot said softly

definitions.text: It could be a sea anemone

indicators.note: said means the word is heard spoken rather than written

parts.note: Polly is the traditional name for a pet parrot
p (piano) is the musical marking for softly

explanation.surface: A parrot quietly saying what a sea creature might be.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea anemone is one form of the simple tube-shaped animal with a ring of tentacles, so it is an example.

clue.text: Cloud borne away in first-class style

indicators.note: away means the letters are carried off and reassembled in another order

explanation.surface: An ash cloud blown away, perhaps carrying passengers in first class.
explanation.definitionFit: Cordon bleu, from a French blue ribbon of honour, describes cookery or anything of the highest class.

clue.text: Made agreeable by dear editor

parts.note: honey is a term of endearment like dear

explanation.surface: An article sweetened by a fond editor.
explanation.definitionFit: Words that are honeyed have been sweetened to sound pleasant and flattering.

clue.text: Wife has tax cut by Switzerland

indicators.note: cut means the word is shortened by its last letter

parts.note: a duty is a tax on goods
CH is the international vehicle code for Switzerland, from Confoederatio Helvetica

explanation.surface: A married woman whose tax bill is reduced by the Swiss authorities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My old Dutch' is Cockney slang for a wife, from 'duchess'.
explanation.definitionFit: In Cockney usage a man calls his spouse his old Dutch, a slang term for a partner in marriage.

clue.text: One that kills headless chicken, potentially?

indicators.note: headless means the first letter is taken away

parts.note: a slayer is a killer

explanation.surface: A question about someone who beheads a chicken, playing on running around like a headless chicken.
explanation.definitionFit: A hen kept for its eggs is a layer, so any chicken might potentially be one.

clue.text: Fly? After initial clearance, leaves from here perhaps

indicators.note: after initial clearance means the opening letter has been cleared away

parts.note: to fly is to rush or dash

explanation.surface: A flight finally cleared to depart after the ash cloud lifted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' suggests a departing flight but means foliage: it is a tree that leaves grow from, while volcanic ash stopped flights.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaves grow on a tree, and this common European tree is one example of where they come from.

clue.text: Until now, hot one — hotter after erupting

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: erupting means the letters burst out into a new order

explanation.surface: A volcano that was already hot has become hotter since it erupted.
explanation.definitionFit: Hitherto is a formal adverb meaning up to this point or until the present.

clue.text: Dismiss European high-flier that's taken cocaine

indicators.note: taken here means the second piece has been taken in by the first

parts.note: a jet flies high
C is slang shorthand for cocaine

explanation.surface: Throwing out a European jet-setter caught taking cocaine.
explanation.definitionFit: To eject someone is to throw them out or expel them, which is to dismiss them.

clue.text: Left with wings clipped — reportedly flew through nasty emissions

indicators.note: with wings clipped means the outer letters on either side are cut off
reportedly means the word is as it would be heard spoken

parts.note: the past tense of fly, spoken like the name of an illness
via means by way of, or through

explanation.surface: A bird with clipped wings that still flew through foul fumes.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking off L and T from 'Left' leaves EF; 'reportedly' turns flew into FLU.
explanation.definitionFit: Effluvia are unpleasant or harmful vapours and discharges given off by something.

clue.text: Instrument, note, is one that plays itself

parts.note: a piano is a keyboard instrument
la (or lah) is the sixth note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A note that a certain musical instrument plays by itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A pianola is a player piano, worked by a perforated roll rather than a pianist.

clue.text: Hancock said his bloody pint was almost this toxic? Not initially

definitions.text: Hancock said his bloody pint was almost this

indicators.note: not initially means the word is used without its first letter

parts.note: something toxic is harmful

explanation.surface: A recollection of a comedian's line about giving blood.
explanation.walkthrough: In the sketch 'The Blood Donor', British comedian Tony Hancock protests that a pint of blood is 'very nearly an armful'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pint of blood is so much that it nearly fills the limb, a quantity Hancock's famous quote exaggerates.

clue.text: Gradual reduction in amount coming from volcano? Extra work towards the end for nerd

indicators.text: Gradual reduction in amount coming from
indicators.note: the number of letters taken from the ends of successive words shrinks step by step: three, then two, then one
towards the end says the letters kept are those at the close of each word

explanation.surface: A volcano that slowly lets out less, and a nerd who puts in overtime at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: Last three of 'volcano' (ANO), last two of 'Extra' (RA), last one of 'work' (K): the takings shrink, which is the 'gradual reduction'.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang an anorak is an obsessive enthusiast, from the waterproof jackets worn by trainspotters.

clue.text: Interval of time before aircraft finally flew back home

indicators.note: back means the word is read in the opposite direction
finally means the last letter is used

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for home, as in sports fixtures

explanation.surface: An interval of time before an aircraft finally flew back to base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Interval' looks like a span of time, but it is the musical sense: the gap of an octave plus a fifth.
explanation.definitionFit: In music a twelfth is the interval spanning an octave and a fifth.

clue.text: Early take-offs from Delta, easyJet, Monarch…oh, and BMI…put out of action

indicators.note: the first letter of each word is taken off it, like a plane taking off early

explanation.surface: Airlines grounded by the 2010 ash cloud, their early departures cancelled.
explanation.definitionFit: To demob, short for demobilise, is to release troops from service, standing them down from action.

clue.text: Owed money for prearranged fight

parts.note: money owed is due
L stands for pounds (Latin librae), i.e. money

explanation.surface: A debt that must be settled by a formal fight.
explanation.definitionFit: A duel is a formal combat between two people, arranged in advance with set rules.

clue.text: All welcome round at top floor flat, taking time out

parts.note: O is round in shape

indicators.note: taking time out means the letter for time is removed

parts.note: a penthouse is a flat on the top floor of a building

explanation.surface: An invitation for everyone to come round to a penthouse flat.
explanation.definitionFit: An open house is hospitality offered to all visitors, where everyone is welcome.

clue.text: Henry joins Bill and Jack for trip to Mecca

parts.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance
an ad (advertisement) is a bill or poster
J is the abbreviation for jack in playing cards

explanation.surface: Three men named Henry, Bill and Jack go on pilgrimage together.
explanation.definitionFit: The hajj or hadj is the Muslim pilgrimage to Mecca, a journey every able Muslim should make.

clue.text: Nobleman taking year off before the appointed time

indicators.note: taking ... off means a piece is removed from the word
off completes the removal signal, the letter taken away

parts.note: early means ahead of schedule

explanation.surface: An aristocrat retiring a year before he was due to.
explanation.definitionFit: An earl is a British peer ranking above a viscount, a titled member of the nobility.

clue.text: In high spirits from energy extra bun produced

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

indicators.note: produced here means made into something new, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone buzzing with energy after an extra bun.
explanation.definitionFit: Exuberant means full of lively energy and cheerful excitement.

clue.text: Less affected by what was in cloud, trapped characters are out of danger? That's right

definitions.text: Less affected by what was in cloud

indicators.note: the letters trapped inside the word are removed, so only its outside ones remain

parts.note: that's means that is, i.e.

explanation.surface: Someone escaping from danger with a cry of 'that's right!'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cloud' invites volcanic ash, but the definition means rain: what a cloud holds.
explanation.definitionFit: Something less wet has had less rain fall on it, rain being the water a cloud contains.
